findings.text: If an 'message' listener throws, emit() throws inside the async loop after shift(). The loop aborts and the rest of the queue is never drained. Later messages see length>1 and return early, so no more messages are emitted. onDisconnect also waits forever on once(ipcEmitter,'message'). Failing input: a throwing listener plus two messages sent back-to-back.

onDisconnect loops on once(ipcEmitter,'message') while the queue is non-empty. If the drain loop is stuck, 'disconnect' is never emitted and connected is never set to false. This happens when the drain loop waits in waitForOutgoingMessages on a send that never settles, or when it has aborted as described above. Failing input: a message is queued and the peer disconnects while a sendMessage is pending.

throwOnEarlyDisconnect no longer takes methodName and now hardcodes 'getOneMessage()'. Any other caller, such as getEachMessage or exchangeMessage, gets a wrong error message. A caller that still passes (methodName, isSubprocess) would pass the method name string as isSubprocess, which is truthy, so it would also report the wrong process side.

The sendOneMessage export is removed and './forward.js' is renamed to './reference.js'. Any remaining importer of sendOneMessage or forward.js, for example an exchangeMessage module, fails at load with a missing export or module. This is unverified, because the patch does not show the other files.

0.reason: A throwing listener aborts the drain loop, leaving the queue stuck and preventing future messages and disconnect handling.

1.reason: onDisconnect waits forever on the message event if the drain loop is stuck or aborted, so disconnect is never emitted.

2.reason: throwOnEarlyDisconnect now hardcodes 'getOneMessage()' and changed its signature, so other callers get wrong error messages or pass methodName as isSubprocess.

3.reason: The patch does not show other modules, so we cannot confirm whether any importer still depends on the removed sendOneMessage export or the renamed forward.js module.
